name: Battle of Mikatagahara

phases.title: The armies take their ground on the plain
phases.text: Ieyasu drew up his forces in a line on the plain of Mikatagahara. Shingen arrayed his men in the fish-scale formation in four lines, with the vanguard first and Baba Nobuharu in the fourth.

phases.title: The Takeda cavalry overruns the Tokugawa right
phases.text: As snow began to fall the Tokugawa arquebusiers opened fire. Naitō Masatoyo's vanguard cavalry attacked all the same and overran Honda Tadakatsu's segment on the Tokugawa right.

phases.title: The Oda reinforcements are routed
phases.text: Takeda horsemen exploited the opening and quickly assaulted the Oda reinforcements, who were overrun and routed. Their officer Hirate Hirohide was killed, and Sakuma Nobumori and Takigawa Kazumasu fled the battle.

phases.title: The Takeda horse charge the Tokugawa rear
phases.text: Having exploited the opening and assaulted the Oda reinforcements, the Takeda horsemen went on to charge the Tokugawa rear, which put them behind the Tokugawa centre.

phases.title: The attack on the Tokugawa left is thrown back
phases.text: A similar attack on the Tokugawa left was thwarted. The Tokugawa units there refused to yield ground and shrugged off the advance of the Takeda right, which prevented an encirclement of the centre.

phases.title: Shingen rests his vanguard and brings up fresh horse
phases.text: Shingen withdrew his vanguard to rest. He brought forward a new set of horsemen from the main body of the army, under Takeda Katsuyori, Obata Masamori and Saegusa Moritomo.

phases.title: A two-pronged charge and the main body break the line
phases.text: The fresh horsemen led a two-pronged cavalry charge into the weakening Tokugawa line, closely followed by the main body. Their combined weight drove the already battered Tokugawa army into a disorderly retreat.

phases.title: Ieyasu flees and his units are overrun
phases.text: Convinced by his retainers that his life was too important, Ieyasu fled the field. Several of his retainers died as their units were encircled and overrun by the Takeda forces.

phases.title: The Takeda vanguard stops short of Hamamatsu
phases.text: Ieyasu returned to Hamamatsu with five men and ordered the gates left open and braziers lit. The Takeda vanguard under Baba Nobuharu and Yamagata Masakage took this for a trap and stopped to make camp for the night short of the town.

phases.title: A night raid throws the Takeda vanguard into confusion
phases.text: A band of about one hundred Tokugawa foot soldiers and 16 matchlock gunners under Ōkubo Tadayo and Amano Yasukage attacked the Takeda camp and threw the vanguard of the Takeda army into confusion.

phases.title: Shingen decides to withdraw
phases.text: Uncertain of the Tokugawa strength, and worried that reinforcements from Oda Nobunaga or Uesugi Kenshin were on their way, Shingen decided to withdraw his forces to his own territories.

note: The Takeda order of battle (four lines in the fish-scale formation) is the one given in the Kōyō Gunkan, a Takeda family record. The accounts do not give the Tokugawa formations' exact places beyond a line with Honda Tadakatsu's segment on the right, a left and a centre, and the Oda reinforcements alongside. The Oda force is placed at the right rear and the arquebusiers in front of the line by judgement. The plain lay just north of Hamamatsu; the Takeda are drawn at the top and the spacing of their lines is schematic. The first and second Takeda lines are drawn as one cavalry body. The Takeda right wing that advanced on the Tokugawa left is not placed in the accounts: it is drawn at its first appearance on the western flank, as cavalry like the other attacks, though the accounts do not say what troops it held.
